NorthWest Election Roadshow - Dysfunction Town

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In debt and disarray, signs show that municipalities in the North West are on the brink of collapse

Unique Selling Point:
Municipalities across the North West province are in complete disarray and local residents are fed up. A local journalist has his finger on the pulse and takes us across different communities where he reports on the issues plaguing small towns and townships. Embroiled in the VBS scandal, water and Eskom debt and a collapse in their administrative function, these municipalities have failed in their constitutional obligation.

Summary:
It's silly season in South African politics and parties are rolling up their sleeves in full campaign mode in the next couple of weeks. Opposition parties are vying for disillusioned voters, promising to pick up the slack dysfunctional municipalities and the ANC will be out in numbers making promises they've previously failed to keep.

The insert will look at the lived experience and reality of residents in Rustenburg through the work of a local radio journalist. No water or often unpurified water has become endemic in the town, Kgaogelo Magelegwa will show us how this problem is affecting both business and residents.


Further information:
It goes without saying that corruption and factionalism in the ruling party has derailed administration in local councils. Brought in in 2018 as the man to clean up the province Prof Job Mogoro will reflect on how he found the state of municipalities when took office as premier and why years later this problem still persists.

Script:



VO UPSOUND VIZ
Aida Maponyana doesn’t have running water. Twice in the morning she walks to a dirty stream to collect water to bath and do house chores.

The streams here are strewn with litter and sometimes sewage, this is not only unsafe for her health but these morning trips are risky.


Clean drinking water is sometimes brought by the municipal truck but often it’s not enough to ration amongst aida and her neighbours
Aida - the mama in the red hat, sitting outside red house. Please use her walking shots and tracking to the river


For the last line please use viz of her almost falling as she steps over stone, walking back home

Find under day 1 wimpie shots
Aida 00;59 - 01;09 sometimes there’s water at six in the morning then by 10 its gone, then it’s back again the following week, when you open the taps, there’s nothing.
01;12 - 01;17 we fill up containers and buckets, so that we can wash dishes and bathe the kids
Irregular water supply is common here. Just 8km from Rustenburg, Boitekong is a sprawling township close to some of the mines in the area. It’s proximity to town and major industry has not translated to its development.

01;16 – 01;33 agness – life in boitekong is not good, we need water, when it hits 5 o’oclock there water is gone, what about the people that work, when they knock they find that there’s no water. What do they bath with, what do they cook with.
Agness is the woman in the floral dress and navy hat.
Agness chipeta is frustrated with the inconvenience of no an intermittent water supply. She’s lived in this neighbourhood since it started in 1992.
Poverty and unemployment are high, and the promise of a better life has been deferred.

Over the years, issues of water supply and basic services has gotten increasingly worse

Agness

01;53 -02;18 agness – and the pipes are broken. When you call the municipality, they say we’ll come, it’s been five months since the water has been leaking. The pipe next to the road, is broken, when you enter boitekong, the pipe is broken, it’s drowning the subcity and the water is just flowing in that area. There’s no development in boitekong.
Kgaogelo- cut-away in studio
‘This is our election special show….’
A news head and politics aficionado, deputy news editor at YOU FM, kgaogelo magolego is out on the ground more than usual this election season,.

In its second year running, the music station broadcasts to some of the smaller towns in the province.

But Kgaugelo is getting his team to cover more news and politics in the north west, following the campaign trail, gathering analysis and getting a special election show on air. He says these coming local polls are overshadowed by national issues.

Driving kgaogelo cut-away
File 00066 MTS
01;18
06; 09 - 07;18
typically they are supposed to be about local issues, they are supposed to be about eh your immediate surrounding, you wanna hear, if you are struggling with a local bridge which hurts your car, or prevents your child from crossing to a school in a near-by village, you wanna hear the candidates as to which one wants to bring a school locally, which one wants to deal with the crime situation, not as you see it on tv but as you experience it where you live. Unfortunately life is not like a movie script, so things don’t happen in a typical form, that’s why you’ll hear so much local politics, what the ANC failed to do over the past 9 years or over the close to 3 decades in power or so, ideally you should be having those local candidates be the ones that are under scrutiny as opposed to their principals who are some where in Pretoria or Cape Town




























File 00067 - kgaogelo getting out of the You Fm car, walking inot street with, ANC people campaignin. File 00068 - ANC man wearing black mask walking, that’s the mayor campaigning
00066 - anc mayor inside house, please note cartoon sound is loud
04;13 I think eh most communities, the north west still looks the way it looked in 2016, it still looks pretty much the way it looked in 2011, the issues of water, electricity and other basic services are still prominent, I think that it is what most people are still struggling with.
With his ear on the ground, i asked him which municipality in his news radar could be considered to be performing and providing basic services.

His response, is frank and candid.




28;03 I can spend weeks trying to find that, sadly there’s none, there’s eh very few. I just painted the bad problems of Rustenburg here and I think it’s ahead of the pack bad as it is, and if Rustenburg is ahead of the pack you can imagine what some 28;24 from a financial management perspective
31;17 so it’s chaos, stories of municipalities struggling to pay salaries have become way too common here and we have not seen municipal managers or mayors losing their jobs over such failures. So we have embraced mediocrity, in a way that’s worrying, it’ll take more than one election to solve it.
A decline in municipal services is detrimental to local economies and development. With potential for growth in industries linked to mines along the platinum belt and surrounding tourist sites, Rustenburg is certainly no a longer small mining town.

It’s population is growing, driving it to become more urbanized.

Simeone du Preez is a local civil engineer that has worked on some of the major construction projects here. From upmarket residential property, retail development sites and roads, he says unmaintained infrastructure has hampered the potential for this town to grow.

















Simeon is the young white man, in an office setting.

Find on site cut-aways in Wimpie;s day 2 shots.
07;13 - 07;40 – the state of Rustenburg and its infrastructure has been on a downward trajectory for quite some time. And we don’t know when the turn around is going to come but if we look at the appetite that local developers have and if we look at the activity from the property market, there’s definitely hope from the residents and from the professionals, that we could see a better future but currently, that’s not the case.
Kgaogelo 10;26 and by the way Rustenburg is aspiring to be a metro, that is why you would see this half done project of a rapid bus transport system here in town, because they, it’s some of the requirements they would need to satisfy in order for them, the necessary regulators to grade them as a metro.
He’s referring to the yarona rapid transit system, introduced almost ten years ago by the Rustenburg Municipality. These are buses that would ferry people around town and surrounding townships. Meaning less traffic on the roads and move people around more efficiently.
